description: Append a falsifiability rule for verification oracles to patterns.md and extend the CLAUDE.md Test-quality invariant with a short pointer clause.

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 001: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: CRITICAL [scripts/cam/prd.json:21]: Two acceptance-criterion oracles are annotated "RED-ON-MAIN (swept)" but measurably return GREEN against unmodified main, so they verify nothing. (1) The keyword-density oracle (criterion 6): `L=$(grep -n 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/patterns.md | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); sed -n "${L}p" ... | grep -qi 'sweep' && ... 'oracle' && ... 'main'`. On main the anchor grep finds nothing, L is the empty string, and `sed -n "p"` degrades to printing the ENTIRE file (measured: 897 lines emitted, not 1); 'sweep', 'oracle' and 'main' all occur somewhere in those 897 lines, so the oracle exits 0 on main. (2) The CLAUDE.md placement oracle (criterion 9): `grep -n 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md | cut -d: -f1 | while read -r n; do ... || exit 1; done`. On main `grep -c falsifiab scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md` is 0, the loop body never executes, and the pipeline exits 0 vacuously. Both were re-run verbatim against a `git show main:` temp tree; evidence in scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt sections 4 and 5. This also falsifies the PRD's own note (9), which claims "every oracle above was swept red against unmodified main except the line-776 pinning oracle and the two house-style oracles". This is the exact defect class the story exists to eliminate, and criterion 9 is the same self-nullifying-oracle family as patterns.md:772/:774 that the new bullet itself cites as precedent. Fix: make both oracles fail closed when the anchor grep finds nothing (e.g. `L=$(...); test -n "$L"` guard, or `grep -c` the loop's match count), and correct any annotation that survives re-measurement.

userStories.title: Review round 1 fix 002: address reviewer finding
userStories.notes: WARNING [scripts/cam/prd.json:19]: Criteria 4, 5, 7, 10 and 11 share the same unguarded empty-`L` construct as the two CRITICAL oracles. They do go red on main, but only incidentally: with L empty they degrade from single-line assertions to whole-file greps, and go red merely because at least one probed token is absent from the whole 897-line file. On the failure path they therefore do NOT enforce the "on its own single line" claim their criterion text makes (a future patterns.md where the tokens are scattered across different lines would satisfy them). Same one-line fix as the CRITICAL: guard `L` non-empty before the `sed -n "${L}p"`.

userStories.title: Add the oracle-falsifiability rule to the knowledge layer
userStories.description: As a subagent-planner authoring acceptance criteria and as a subagent-implementer authoring test assertions, I need a durable, greppable rule requiring every verification oracle to be proven red against unmodified main via an exhaustive sweep, so that tautological oracles like CAM-363, CAM-368 and CAM-374 stop reaching a PRD or a test file.
acceptanceCriteria: RED-ON-MAIN (swept, main returns 0): the falsifiability rule exists in patterns.md. [oracle: test "$(grep -c 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/patterns.md)" -ge 1]

RED-ON-MAIN (swept, main has no match at all): the new bullet is appended strictly BELOW every pre-existing bullet (patterns.md is 897 lines on main, final bullet at line 897). [oracle: test "$(grep -n 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/patterns.md | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)" -gt 897]

PINNING ORACLE, deliberately GREEN-ON-MAIN (regression guard on invariance, not a claim about new behavior, exempt from the red-first duty by that fact): no pre-existing line shifted, so the many patterns.md:NNN cross-references elsewhere in the file remain valid. [oracle: sed -n '776p' scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -q 'Test-quality convention, expanded']

RED-ON-MAIN (swept): the new bullet cites all three precedents on its own single line. [oracle: L=$(grep -n 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/patterns.md | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -q 'CAM-363' && sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -q 'CAM-368' && sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -q 'CAM-374']

RED-ON-MAIN (swept): the new bullet covers BOTH authoring surfaces, PRD acceptance criteria and in-test assertions, not just PRDs. [oracle: L=$(grep -n 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/patterns.md | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -qi 'acceptance' && sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -qi 'test assertion']

RED-ON-MAIN (swept, guarded fail-closed on an empty anchor): the new bullet is keyword-dense enough to be found by a future flat-file grep, carrying the sweep-vs-sample and red-against-main language. [oracle: L=$(grep -n 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/patterns.md | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); test -n "$L" && sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -qi 'sweep' && sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -qi 'oracle' && sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -qi 'main']

RED-ON-MAIN (swept): the new bullet back-references adjacent precedent bullets by line pointer in the established house style, naming patterns.md:776 and at least one of the CAM-236 sweep-completeness cluster (:566, :570, :572) or the CAM-301/CAM-309 self-nullifying-oracle antipattern (:772, :774). [oracle: L=$(grep -n 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/patterns.md | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -q 'patterns.md:776' && sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -qE 'patterns\.md:(566|570|572|772|774)']
RED-ON-MAIN (swept, main returns 0): the curated invariants block in scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md gains a short falsifiability clause. [oracle: test "$(grep -c 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md)" -ge 1]

RED-ON-MAIN (swept, guarded fail-closed on a zero match count): that CLAUDE.md clause lives INSIDE the existing 'Test quality' bullet rather than as a new standalone invariant bullet. [oracle: N=$(grep -c 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md); test "$N" -ge 1 && grep -n 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md | cut -d: -f1 | while read -r n; do test "$n" = "$(grep -n '^- \*\*Test quality\*\*' scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md | head -1 | cut -d: -f1)" || exit 1; done]

HOUSE STYLE, conditional on the first criterion having matched (vacuously true if it fails, so meaningful only read together with it): the new patterns.md bullet is a single unwrapped line starting with `- **`. [oracle: L=$(grep -n 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/patterns.md | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -q '^- \*\*']

HOUSE STYLE: the new patterns.md bullet carries no `[resolved` prefix and no em-dash character, per the no-em-dash-in-persisted-md rule at patterns.md:24. [oracle: L=$(grep -n 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/patterns.md | head -1 | cut -d: -f1); ! sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -q '\[resolved' && ! sed -n "${L}p" scripts/cam/patterns.md | grep -q '—']
No src/ or test/ file is modified by this story (doc-only scope). [oracle: test -z "$(git diff --name-only main...HEAD -- src test)"]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test), zero failures with the count at or above main's baseline. [oracle: bun test]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: scripts/cam/patterns.md (APPEND AT EOF ONLY, currently 897 lines) and scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md (extend the existing 'Test quality' bullet at line 69, in place, short form + pointer to patterns.md). GOTCHAS: (1) patterns.md has NO sections: it is a `# Codebase Patterns` heading, a 6-line preamble, then a flat blank-line-separated list of top-level `- ` bullets to EOF. Agent docs saying 'grep for the section' rest on a false premise; discovery is pure keyword grep, so the new bullet must be KEYWORD-DENSE (falsifiable, oracle, acceptance criterion, grep, test assertion, sweep, main). (2) Many bullets cross-reference other bullets BY LINE NUMBER (patterns.md:20, :150, :324, :454, :770, :776 and others). Inserting anywhere except EOF silently invalidates every pointer; that is what the deliberately green-on-main line-776 pinning oracle guards. (3) Do NOT amend the line-776 test-quality bullet: it carries a pre-existing 'Four clauses' vs five-clauses off-by-one that is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE, and editing it shifts every subsequent line number. Back-reference it instead. (4) Do NOT touch test/dispatch.test.ts: the weak assertion there is CAM-374, a separate issue and a separate PR. (5) Never prefix a living rule with `[resolved YYYY-MM]`: `cam patterns archive` sweeps any bullet carrying it into patterns.archive.md, and patterns.md currently has zero such markers. (6) No file-size budget applies: scripts/check-file-sizes.ts:96 globs `{src,scripts,test}/**/*.{ts,tsx}` with no .md handling, so no budget raise and no tracker-ref ceremony. (7) No vendor/templates change, so `bun run embed-vendor:check` is not in scope; verified there is no template dual-copy of scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md (grep -rl 'Test quality' matches only that file). (8) Generalize, do not restate, the nearby oracle-CORRECTNESS bullets (:772/:774 self-nullifying `-q` + `-L`/`-l`, :616 structurally unsatisfiable file-count oracles, :412/:842/:588 negative-grep matching comments, and the CAM-236 sweep-completeness cluster at :566/:570/:572); this bullet is about oracle FALSIFIABILITY, which is genuinely new language (`grep falsifiab` returns 0 on main for both files). (9) [CORRECTED by US-R1-001, 2026-07-20: this annotation was itself wrong, see scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt sections 4-5] The rule applies recursively to this PRD: every oracle above except the line-776 pinning oracle and the two house-style oracles (both exempt and labelled inline) was INTENDED to be swept red against unmodified main, but criteria 6 and 9 as originally written were non-falsifiable (an unguarded empty anchor variable degrades `sed -n "${L}p"` to whole-file printing, and an unguarded empty match set makes a `while read` loop vacuously true), so they returned GREEN on unmodified main instead of RED; both were fixed in place by US-R1-001 to fail closed on an empty anchor.

findings.text: Two acceptance-criterion oracles are annotated "RED-ON-MAIN (swept)" but measurably return GREEN against unmodified main, so they verify nothing. (2) The CLAUDE.md placement oracle (criterion 9): `grep -n 'falsifiab' scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md | cut -d: -f1 | while read -r n; do ... || exit 1; done`. On main `grep -c falsifiab scripts/cam/CLAUDE.md` is 0, the loop body never executes, and the pipeline exits 0 vacuously. Both were re-run verbatim against a `git show main:` temp tree; evidence in scripts/cam/review-artifact.txt sections 4 and 5. This is the exact defect class the story exists to eliminate, and criterion 9 is the same self-nullifying-oracle family as patterns.md:772/:774 that the new bullet itself cites as precedent. Fix: make both oracles fail closed when the anchor grep finds nothing (e.g. `L=$(...); test -n "$L"` guard, or `grep -c` the loop's match count), and correct any annotation that survives re-measurement.

Criteria 4, 5, 7, 10 and 11 share the same unguarded empty-`L` construct as the two CRITICAL oracles. They do go red on main, but only incidentally: with L empty they degrade from single-line assertions to whole-file greps, and go red merely because at least one probed token is absent from the whole 897-line file. Same one-line fix as the CRITICAL: guard `L` non-empty before the `sed -n "${L}p"`.

Criterion 2 hardcodes the magic number 897 (`test ... -gt 897`) as main's line count. This is correct today but becomes silently wrong the moment another PRD appends to patterns.md before this one merges. Deriving the baseline (`git show main:scripts/cam/patterns.md | wc -l`) would keep the append-at-EOF intent load-bearing across rebases.

The new bullet is a single ~1100-character line. That matches the file's established house style and the flat-file grep discovery model, so it is correct as written; noting only that the cited precedent bullets (:772, :774) are appreciably shorter, and a future reader scanning raw would find the three-precedent enumeration (CAM-363/368/374) easier to parse if the causal clause led rather than trailed.
